steps.what: Design special supplies or specify suitable adaptive equipment
Create or requisition the specified supplies and check individual fit

tasks.design: Retain individual design, fabrication or requisition and fit checks with the therapist. Existing {DOCS} specifications may support the work; the digest establishes no validated adaptive-equipment design or fabrication saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: Physical fit and individual function determine whether equipment is suitable.
tasks.enabler_now: No new capability is assumed for this task.
tasks.still_hard: Pressure, comfort, functional limitations and safe use in context.
tasks.human_edge: Observe fit and use, then modify the intervention.
tasks.altitude: Equipment decisions and hands-on time remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Recognise when specialist fitting expertise is required

evidence.claim: Adaptive equipment suitability depends on individual assessment and fit; no relevant validated replacement is documented in the digest.

assumptions: Boundary is therapist specification and provision. Creation and requisition are alternative routes within s2, not sequential duplicated work; supplier manufacturing is excluded.
Therapist produces measurements and specification in s1 with capture time retained. No structured body model or machine-ready device design is assumed.
Test native specification records before custom tools. The unchanged process adds no upkeep.
research_questions: Which equipment routes contain measurable repeated entry separate from assessment and fitting?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=40+60=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. Specification, applicable creation or requisition route, and individual fit retain all effort; no assumed paperwork saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Assess patients' work or living environments against needs and capabilities
Recommend feasible environmental changes with the patient

tasks.design: Keep environmental assessment and patient-specific recommendations with the therapist. Existing {DOCS} guidance supports discussion without replacing inspection or practical feasibility judgement.
tasks.previous_blocker: The same adaptation can help one person and create barriers for another.
tasks.enabler_now: No validated environment-assessment automation is supplied in this digest.
tasks.still_hard: Balancing independence, cost, consent and physical constraints.
tasks.human_edge: Understand daily routines and negotiate acceptable changes.
tasks.altitude: Advisory authority and assessment time remain unchanged.

reach.task: Assess movement implications of environmental changes

evidence.claim: Individual environmental assessment and recommendations remain human work in this design; no measured saving is supplied.

assumptions: Boundary includes therapist environmental assessment and recommendations, excluding building work and separate equipment fitting.
Therapist produces observed barriers in s1 with all observation time retained; no structured room model or inferred accessibility compliance is assumed.
Use existing guidance access first. Unchanged work adds zero incremental upkeep.
research_questions: Which barriers are apparent only during the patient's real activities?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=55+45=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. Observation and negotiated recommendations retain all time; no reporting component is invented.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Develop and deliver health promotion activities

steps.what: Develop health promotion programmes and group activities for client needs
Participate in group activities and discussions promoting client health and adjustment

tasks.design: Retain clinical programme development and direct group participation. The {DOCS} programme is a working plan; this broad task does not establish a repetitive material-authoring component that can safely be assigned a saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: Appropriate activities depend on group needs, stressors and participation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing planning documents support practice without a claimed breakthrough.
tasks.still_hard: Responding to distress and adapting activities to changing group interaction.
tasks.human_edge: Facilitate belonging, observe response and adjust support.
tasks.altitude: Programme judgement and client-facing time remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Combine participation goals with individual support needs

evidence.claim: Clinical programme development and direct group facilitation retain their effort here; generic drafting capability does not establish a task-specific saving.

assumptions: Boundary is therapist programme design and participation; client time and separate service delivery by colleagues are excluded.
Therapist produces the programme in s1, retaining assessment and planning effort. No structured client classification or automatic programme assignment is assumed.
Check native planning templates first. This unchanged service creates no incremental upkeep.
research_questions: How much programme development is reusable wording versus clinical adaptation?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=40+60=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. Programme judgement and live participation remain intact; reuse alone earns no unmeasured labour saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Train and supervise care staff in therapy techniques

steps.what: Provide training and supervision in therapy techniques and objectives

tasks.design: Keep practical training, observation and supervision with the therapist. Existing {DOCS} technique guides support teaching; a guide cannot establish that a learner performs a technique safely.
tasks.previous_blocker: Competence and clinical reasoning require observation and feedback.
tasks.enabler_now: No new validated training substitute is established in the digest.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising unsafe practice and tailoring feedback to experience.
tasks.human_edge: Demonstrate, coach and decide when closer supervision is needed.
tasks.altitude: Training responsibility and supervision time remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Agree competence limits and escalation conditions

evidence.claim: Practical observation and supervision remain human work; document access does not replace competence assessment.

assumptions: Boundary is therapist training and supervision, excluding learner attendance and subsequent independent practice.
Therapist observes performance during the fully counted step; no structured competence flags or automated certification are assumed.
Use existing training references before new systems. Retained teaching introduces zero incremental upkeep.
research_questions: What observable performance indicates the learner can safely apply each technique?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. Practical demonstration, supervision and feedback retain all therapist time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Equipment provision, environmental adaptation, group work and practical supervision retain their human and physical scope.
reach: Seek specialist fit advice from orthotists and prosthetists
Coordinate practical teaching with registered nurses
Share participation approaches with recreational therapists
role.ambitious_version: An occupational therapist whose week remains centred on individual function, usable adaptations and safe practical learning.
